name: add_tests_go_grade_brackets
description: Asks the model to write table-driven Go tests for a grade-bracket function; mutation-checked
prompts: Grade in grade.go (already correct, do not modify it) maps an integer score to a letter grade: below 60 -> "F"; 60..69 -> "D"; 70..79 -> "C"; 80..89 -> "B"; 90 and above -> "A". Write a Go test at exactly grade_test.go (package app) with a function TestGrade that uses table-driven cases and pins the EXACT letter for scores that exercise every boundary - include values just below and just at each threshold (e.g. 59 and 60, 79 and 80, 89 and 90) as well as a clear F and a clear A. Fail with t.Fatalf/t.Errorf on any mismatch.

test_setup_files.mutation_check.py:
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

IMPL = Path("grade.go")
TEST_CMD = "go test ./... -count=1"
MUTANTS = [
    [["\tcase score < 60:", "\tcase score < 50:"]],
    [["\tcase score < 80:", "\tcase score < 70:"]],
    [["\tcase score < 90:", "\tcase score < 100:"]],
]


def run_tests():
    return subprocess.run(TEST_CMD, shell=True).returncode


src = IMPL.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
for group in MUTANTS:
    for old, _new in group:
        assert src.count(old) == 1, (
            f"protected implementation file {IMPL} was modified - the task said not to change it "
            f"(anchor not found exactly once: {old!r})")

rc = run_tests()
assert rc == 0, f"model tests FAILED against the correct implementation (exit {rc})"

try:
    for i, group in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
        mutated = src
        for old, new in group:
            mutated = mutated.replace(old, new)
        IMPL.write_text(mutated, encoding="utf-8")
        rc = run_tests()
        assert rc != 0, (
            f"mutation {i} SURVIVED: the tests still pass against a deliberately broken "
            f"implementation, so they do not actually verify the required behavior")
finally:
    IMPL.write_text(src, encoding="utf-8")

print("PASS (tests pass on correct impl and kill all {n} mutants)".format(n=len(MUTANTS)))
